principles.instruction: Project every relation onto the supplied predicted-entity inventory. A relation endpoint must be the ID of one supplied predicted entity; never invent an ID, create a composite span, or return a human-annotation ID.
principles.applies_when: Selecting or aligning either endpoint of any relation.
exceptions: Minor punctuation or boundary differences may be normalized when a predicted entity clearly denotes the same concept.
A predicted entity may be used despite an observation-label disagreement if its span and concept clearly match.

If an annotated multiword endpoint is split into several predicted entities, select the single semantic head appropriate to the relation. Additional modifier-to-head relations may be emitted only when independently licensed by the text.
If no predicted entity represents a required endpoint, omit that relation rather than substituting a neighboring entity or collapsing a relation path.
examples: A location spanning a regional qualifier plus an organ maps to the supplied organ-head entity, while the regional qualifier may separately Modify the organ.
If a positional predicate is not supplied as an entity, do not replace it with the finding and manufacture a direct positional relation.

principles.instruction: Emit directed triples with exactly one allowed predicate: LocatedAt, Modify, or SuggestiveOf. Preserve subject and object roles; do not add inverse, symmetric, or transitive relations. Emit an exact triple only once.
principles.applies_when: Formatting and validating all relation outputs.
exceptions: The same endpoint pair may receive different predicates only when distinct textual semantics independently support both labels.
Repeated mentions in different sentences or report sections are separate entities and may receive analogous relations without being duplicates.
examples: A finding-to-organ location does not license the inverse organ-to-finding triple.
A qualifier-to-finding relation and a finding-to-site relation form a path; they do not imply qualifier-to-site.

principles.instruction: For a standalone, unmodified, adjective-first verbless sentence in the FINDINGS section consisting only of a state observation immediately followed by an anatomical noun, emit LocatedAt from the anatomical entity to the state entity; otherwise retain the canonical hosted finding/state/device -> anatomical host direction.
principles.applies_when: The local FINDINGS sentence has the complete form "<state observation> <anatomy>." with no copula, coordination, anatomical modifier, or other supplied content entity.
exceptions: Copular or anatomy-first predications retain state -> anatomy direction.
Adjective-first fragments containing laterality, regional qualifiers, coordination, or additional content retain state -> anatomy direction.
Summary or IMPRESSION restatements retain state -> anatomy direction.
examples: In the standalone FINDINGS fragment "Clear lungs.", emit lungs -> Clear.
For the IMPRESSION fragment "Clear lungs.", emit Clear -> lungs.

principles.instruction: Represent anatomical phrases compositionally. When selecting the LocatedAt object from a phrase containing an anatomy-bearing owner or descriptor plus a generic depiction/container noun such as contour, silhouette, region, or zone, attach the observation to the anatomy-bearing entity rather than the generic noun. Continue to attach anatomical qualifiers to their head with Modify when independently licensed.
principles.applies_when: A LocatedAt candidate has competing supplied objects within the same anatomical noun phrase, and one candidate identifies the anatomy while another merely names its generic depiction or regional container.
exceptions: Use a specific anatomical head such as lobe, spine, atrium, or hemidiaphragm when it is the actual asserted site; laterality or directional modifiers do not displace such a head solely because they are closer.

Retain the generic property/component as object when the subject explicitly denotes a property-specific measurement or alteration of that component, such as an enlarged silhouette; scalar property predications involving size or volume remain governed by R06.

Do not attach the observation to a distant anatomy mentioned in a proximity phrase such as "near the hilum" when the observation is locally anchored to an anatomy-bearing descriptor in its own noun phrase.

," emit normal -> cardiac rather than normal -> contour.

," retain opacity -> lobe because lobe is a specific anatomical site.

The entities occur as components of the same explicit "

exceptions: Emit only edges whose endpoints are supplied entities, and do not infer analogous edges across clauses or sentences.
Do not reverse these edges to normal -> limits or normal -> within.

$iu_join: " licenses within -> normal and limits -> normal.

examples: If only "within" and "normal" are supplied, emit only within -> normal.

exceptions: Telegraphic predications such as "heart size normal" count as explicit predicative constructions even when the copula is omitted.
A shared predicate may license LocatedAt to each coordinated property clearly within its grammatical scope.
Explicit spatial placement of a device component remains eligible for LocatedAt under the ordinary destination rule.
Modifiers of findings that are not anatomical property/component nouns remain governed by the ordinary Modify rules.

principles.instruction: Attach each explicit modifier to the semantic or grammatical head of its phrase rather than to the nearest compatible entity. Parallel prenominal qualifiers skip intervening qualifiers and share the phrase head, while genuinely nested qualifiers form a scope chain. When a phrase-level or property modifier occurs in an anatomical phrase containing a semantically transparent depiction/container noun such as silhouette or region plus an explicit anatomy-bearing owner or more specific appositive head, use that anatomy-bearing entity as the Modify object.

principles.instruction: Use SuggestiveOf for an explicit evidential or interpretive link from an observed sign, finding, structure, or state to a possible diagnosis, explanation, consequence, or clinical interpretation. Resolve an omitted evidence source to the immediately preceding finding when an adjacent inferential sentence uses a demonstrative, ellipsis, or contrastive alternative without introducing a new source; when a postposed inferential phrase scopes over a coordinated evidence phrase, emit the relation from each eligible conjunct.
principles.applies_when: The text uses an inferential construction equivalent to suggesting, representing, being consistent with, demonstrating, possibly being, or having uncertain significance, including a locally continued interpretation whose source is anaphoric or shared across coordinated evidence entities.
exceptions: The target should normally be an observation or interpretive entity, not a purely anatomical entity.
Do not resolve an omitted source across a section boundary, beyond the immediately adjacent inferential sequence, or when a new source or competing antecedent intervenes.
Do not extend a postposed interpretation to nearby entities outside the coordinated source phrase or when punctuation or an independent clause explicitly restricts it to one conjunct.
An anatomical source is permitted when the anatomy or its appearance is explicitly placed within the inferential scope.
Do not use SuggestiveOf for recommendations, follow-up examinations, or mere co-occurrence.

$iu_join: ," emit opacity -> artifactual and opacity -> nodule.
," emit shoulder -> amputation and humerus -> amputation.

examples: In "opacities could represent pneumonia," emit opacities -> pneumonia.

principles.instruction: For an explicit inferential statement with alternatives, emit one SuggestiveOf relation from the stated source to each eligible supplied interpretive target.
principles.applies_when: One finding is explicitly said to represent, suggest, or be consistent with multiple alternatives.
exceptions: Do not create a SuggestiveOf edge to an alternative represented only by an anatomical entity.
A bare list joined by an ambiguity marker is insufficient when no explicit source finding and inferential predicate are present.
If only one alternative has a usable supplied entity, emit only that projectable relation.
examples: single imaging finding -> first possible diagnosis and single imaging finding -> second possible diagnosis

s a condition, retain only the condition as a SuggestiveOf target.

principles.instruction: Relation annotation is independent of assertion status. Preserve valid LocatedAt, Modify, and SuggestiveOf links for present, absent, uncertain, stable, or negated findings.
principles.applies_when: A relation-bearing phrase occurs under negation, uncertainty, or an absence label.
exceptions: Negation does not by itself license a relation; the underlying semantic link must still be explicit.
Do not convert negation words into relation endpoints unless they are supplied entities and function as genuine modifiers.
examples: absent effusion -> pleural compartment
acute qualifier -> absent abnormality
absent opacities -> possible diagnosis when the sentence explicitly states what such opacities would suggest

principles.instruction: Resolve shared scope conservatively. A common state or modifier may relate to multiple coordinated entities when grammar clearly places all conjuncts within its scope.
principles.applies_when: A predicate follows or precedes a coordinated list of findings, structures, or properties.
exceptions: Do not extend the predicate to a nearby entity outside the coordination.
Do not assume that a relation applying to one repeated finding automatically applies to all other mentions.
examples: one normality state -> each explicitly coordinated organ property
one unremarkable state -> each member of an anatomical list
one finding -> general site and a more specific site when both are explicitly asserted

principles.instruction: Keep relation resolution local. Prefer entities in the same noun phrase, clause, or explicit predicate-argument construction, and do not perform unsupported cross-sentence or cross-section coreference.
principles.applies_when: A possible relation would require resolving a pronoun, an omitted noun, a distant repeated concept, or an antecedent in another section.
exceptions: Repeated findings in a summary section may be annotated independently using the entities and wording present in that section.
A relation may cross a short clause boundary only when the source and target are explicitly connected by the sentence's grammar.
examples: Do not connect an earlier lesion to a later diagnosis expressed only through an unannotated pronoun.
Annotate a repeated summary finding with its own summary-site entity rather than linking it to the earlier site mention.

principles.instruction: When a supplied positional or projection predicate is an entity, preserve it as an intermediate relation node. Link the positional predicate to its anatomical destination with LocatedAt, and use Modify for its direct compositional attachment to the finding or device component.
principles.applies_when: The text contains a supplied entity corresponding to projecting, overlying, or another positional relation.
exceptions: Do not collapse the path into a direct finding-to-site relation unless the text independently states that direct location.
If the positional entity is unavailable, omit relations requiring it rather than replacing it with an adjacent entity.
Use the grammatical descriptive dependency for the Modify edge; do not infer both directions.
examples: positional predicate -> destination structure via LocatedAt
positional predicate -> device tip via Modify when the predicate describes the tip
finding and positional predicate form a compositional edge only when both are supplied entities

principles.instruction: Choose the predicate by semantic precedence: explicit diagnostic interpretation selects SuggestiveOf; explicit spatial or host anchoring selects LocatedAt; descriptive or compositional dependence selects Modify.
principles.applies_when: A candidate pair appears compatible with more than one relation label.
exceptions: Multiple labels may be retained only if separate explicit constructions support separate meanings.
Entity labels alone never determine the predicate.
Corpus-specific direction anomalies should not override the dominant semantic direction unless the local text unambiguously requires it.
examples: A lesion described as nodular receives Modify from the morphology term, but a possible nodule interpretation receives SuggestiveOf.
An anatomical adjective on a lesion is a location anchor, whereas the same adjective on an anatomical head is a modifier.

principles.instruction: Avoid relation overgeneration. Do not annotate mere adjacency, shared topic, comparison with a prior study, examination recommendations, notification statements, or transitive consequences of already emitted relations.
principles.applies_when: No explicit grammatical, spatial, descriptive, or inferential link connects two supplied entities.
exceptions: Measurements and explicit temporal-status descriptors are valid Modify relations.
Explicit report-summary restatements are valid independent relation contexts.
examples: A recommended imaging region is not automatically related to the finding prompting the recommendation.
A modifier attached to a finding does not inherit the finding's anatomical location.
Two findings listed in the same sentence receive no relation solely because they co-occur.

principles.instruction: Do not emit Modify when the subject functions only as an epistemic or metalinguistic assessment of a concept's reality, determinacy, or clinical significance rather than as a descriptive attribute of that concept.
principles.applies_when: A supplied term such as "true," "indeterminate," or "unknown" qualifies whether a finding is real or interpretable, or comments on its clinical significance.
exceptions: Retain Modify for explicit morphology, measurement, severity, temporal status, and scalar degree descriptors, including terms such as rounded, nodular, stable, significant, and borderline.
This rule does not suppress a relation independently licensed by an explicit descriptive use of the same word.

exceptions: Retain separate relations when either the source head or target head differs, or when the later occurrence expresses a distinct interpretation rather than a restatement.

principles.applies_when: The text uses an inferential construction equivalent to suggesting, representing, being consistent with, demonstrating, possibly being, or having uncertain significance, including a locally continued interpretation whose source is anaphoric or shared across coordinated evidence entities.
exceptions: The target should normally be an observation or interpretive entity, not a purely anatomical entity.
Do not resolve an omitted source across a section boundary, beyond the immediately adjacent inferential sequence, or when a new source or competing antecedent intervenes.
Do not extend a postposed interpretation to nearby entities outside the coordinated source phrase or when punctuation or an independent clause explicitly restricts it to one conjunct.
An anatomical source is permitted when the anatomy or its appearance is explicitly placed within the inferential scope.
Do not use SuggestiveOf for recommendations, follow-up examinations, or mere co-occurrence.

principles.applies_when: One finding is explicitly said to represent, suggest, or be consistent with multiple alternatives.
exceptions: Do not create a SuggestiveOf edge to an alternative represented only by an anatomical entity.
A bare list joined by an ambiguity marker is insufficient when no explicit source finding and inferential predicate are present.
If only one alternative has a usable supplied entity, emit only that projectable relation.
examples: single imaging finding -> first possible diagnosis and single imaging finding -> second possible diagnosis

principles.instruction: Relation annotation is independent of assertion status. Preserve valid LocatedAt, Modify, and SuggestiveOf links for present, absent, uncertain, stable, or negated findings.
principles.applies_when: A relation-bearing phrase occurs under negation, uncertainty, or an absence label.
exceptions: Negation does not by itself license a relation; the underlying semantic link must still be explicit.
Do not convert negation words into relation endpoints unless they are supplied entities and function as genuine modifiers.
examples: absent effusion -> pleural compartment
acute qualifier -> absent abnormality
absent opacities -> possible diagnosis when the sentence explicitly states what such opacities would suggest

principles.instruction: Resolve shared scope conservatively. A common state or modifier may relate to multiple coordinated entities when grammar clearly places all conjuncts within its scope.
principles.applies_when: A predicate follows or precedes a coordinated list of findings, structures, or properties.
exceptions: Do not extend the predicate to a nearby entity outside the coordination.
Do not assume that a relation applying to one repeated finding automatically applies to all other mentions.
examples: one normality state -> each explicitly coordinated organ property
one unremarkable state -> each member of an anatomical list
one finding -> general site and a more specific site when both are explicitly asserted

principles.instruction: Keep relation resolution local. Prefer entities in the same noun phrase, clause, or explicit predicate-argument construction, and do not perform unsupported cross-sentence or cross-section coreference.
principles.applies_when: A possible relation would require resolving a pronoun, an omitted noun, a distant repeated concept, or an antecedent in another section.
exceptions: Repeated findings in a summary section may be annotated independently using the entities and wording present in that section.
A relation may cross a short clause boundary only when the source and target are explicitly connected by the sentence's grammar.
examples: Do not connect an earlier lesion to a later diagnosis expressed only through an unannotated pronoun.
Annotate a repeated summary finding with its own summary-site entity rather than linking it to the earlier site mention.

principles.instruction: When a supplied positional or projection predicate is an entity, preserve it as an intermediate relation node. Link the positional predicate to its anatomical destination with LocatedAt, and use Modify for its direct compositional attachment to the finding or device component.
principles.applies_when: The text contains a supplied entity corresponding to projecting, overlying, or another positional relation.
exceptions: Do not collapse the path into a direct finding-to-site relation unless the text independently states that direct location.
If the positional entity is unavailable, omit relations requiring it rather than replacing it with an adjacent entity.
Use the grammatical descriptive dependency for the Modify edge; do not infer both directions.
examples: positional predicate -> destination structure via LocatedAt
positional predicate -> device tip via Modify when the predicate describes the tip
finding and positional predicate form a compositional edge only when both are supplied entities

principles.instruction: Choose the predicate by semantic precedence: explicit diagnostic interpretation selects SuggestiveOf; explicit spatial or host anchoring selects LocatedAt; descriptive or compositional dependence selects Modify.
principles.applies_when: A candidate pair appears compatible with more than one relation label.
exceptions: Multiple labels may be retained only if separate explicit constructions support separate meanings.
Entity labels alone never determine the predicate.
Corpus-specific direction anomalies should not override the dominant semantic direction unless the local text unambiguously requires it.
examples: A lesion described as nodular receives Modify from the morphology term, but a possible nodule interpretation receives SuggestiveOf.
An anatomical adjective on a lesion is a location anchor, whereas the same adjective on an anatomical head is a modifier.

principles.instruction: Avoid relation overgeneration. Do not annotate mere adjacency, shared topic, comparison with a prior study, examination recommendations, notification statements, or transitive consequences of already emitted relations.

Explicit report-summary restatements are valid independent relation contexts.
examples: A recommended imaging region is not automatically related to the finding prompting the recommendation.
A modifier attached to a finding does not inherit the finding's anatomical location.
Two findings listed in the same sentence receive no relation solely because they co-occur.

exceptions: Negation does not by itself license a relation; the underlying semantic link must still be explicit.
Do not convert negation words into relation endpoints unless they are supplied entities and function as genuine modifiers.
examples: absent effusion -> pleural compartment
acute qualifier -> absent abnormality
absent opacities -> possible diagnosis when the sentence explicitly states what such opacities would suggest

current_principles.instruction: Resolve shared scope conservatively. A common state or modifier may relate to multiple coordinated entities when grammar clearly places all conjuncts within its scope.
current_principles.applies_when: A predicate follows or precedes a coordinated list of findings, structures, or properties.
exceptions: Do not extend the predicate to a nearby entity outside the coordination.
Do not assume that a relation applying to one repeated finding automatically applies to all other mentions.
examples: one normality state -> each explicitly coordinated organ property
one unremarkable state -> each member of an anatomical list
one finding -> general site and a more specific site when both are explicitly asserted

current_principles.instruction: Keep relation resolution local. Prefer entities in the same noun phrase, clause, or explicit predicate-argument construction, and do not perform unsupported cross-sentence or cross-section coreference.
current_principles.applies_when: A possible relation would require resolving a pronoun, an omitted noun, a distant repeated concept, or an antecedent in another section.
exceptions: Repeated findings in a summary section may be annotated independently using the entities and wording present in that section.
A relation may cross a short clause boundary only when the source and target are explicitly connected by the sentence's grammar.
examples: Do not connect an earlier lesion to a later diagnosis expressed only through an unannotated pronoun.
Annotate a repeated summary finding with its own summary-site entity rather than linking it to the earlier site mention.

current_principles.instruction: When a supplied positional or projection predicate is an entity, preserve it as an intermediate relation node. Link the positional predicate to its anatomical destination with LocatedAt, and use Modify for its direct compositional attachment to the finding or device component.
current_principles.applies_when: The text contains a supplied entity corresponding to projecting, overlying, or another positional relation.
exceptions: Do not collapse the path into a direct finding-to-site relation unless the text independently states that direct location.
If the positional entity is unavailable, omit relations requiring it rather than replacing it with an adjacent entity.
Use the grammatical descriptive dependency for the Modify edge; do not infer both directions.
examples: positional predicate -> destination structure via LocatedAt
positional predicate -> device tip via Modify when the predicate describes the tip
finding and positional predicate form a compositional edge only when both are supplied entities

current_principles.instruction: Choose the predicate by semantic precedence: explicit diagnostic interpretation selects SuggestiveOf; explicit spatial or host anchoring selects LocatedAt; descriptive or compositional dependence selects Modify.
current_principles.applies_when: A candidate pair appears compatible with more than one relation label.
exceptions: Multiple labels may be retained only if separate explicit constructions support separate meanings.
Entity labels alone never determine the predicate.
Corpus-specific direction anomalies should not override the dominant semantic direction unless the local text unambiguously requires it.
examples: A lesion described as nodular receives Modify from the morphology term, but a possible nodule interpretation receives SuggestiveOf.
An anatomical adjective on a lesion is a location anchor, whereas the same adjective on an anatomical head is a modifier.

current_principles.instruction: Avoid relation overgeneration. Do not annotate mere adjacency, shared topic, comparison with a prior study, examination recommendations, notification statements, or transitive consequences of already emitted relations.
current_principles.applies_when: No explicit grammatical, spatial, descriptive, or inferential link connects two supplied entities.
exceptions: Measurements and explicit temporal-status descriptors are valid Modify relations.
Explicit report-summary restatements are valid independent relation contexts.
examples: A recommended imaging region is not automatically related to the finding prompting the recommendation.
A modifier attached to a finding does not inherit the finding's anatomical location.
Two findings listed in the same sentence receive no relation solely because they co-occur.

exceptions: Retain Modify for explicit morphology, measurement, severity, temporal status, and scalar degree descriptors, including terms such as rounded, nodular, stable, significant, and borderline.

principles.instruction: Project every relation onto the supplied predicted-entity inventory. A relation endpoint must be the ID of one supplied predicted entity; never invent an ID, create a composite span, or return a human-annotation ID.
principles.applies_when: Selecting or aligning either endpoint of any relation.
exceptions: Minor punctuation or boundary differences may be normalized when a predicted entity clearly denotes the same concept.
A predicted entity may be used despite an observation-label disagreement if its span and concept clearly match.

examples: A location spanning a regional qualifier plus an organ maps to the supplied organ-head entity, while the regional qualifier may separately Modify the organ.

principles.instruction: Emit directed triples with exactly one allowed predicate: LocatedAt, Modify, or SuggestiveOf. Preserve subject and object roles; do not add inverse, symmetric, or transitive relations. Emit an exact triple only once.
principles.applies_when: Formatting and validating all relation outputs.
exceptions: The same endpoint pair may receive different predicates only when distinct textual semantics independently support both labels.
Repeated mentions in different sentences or report sections are separate entities and may receive analogous relations without being duplicates.
examples: A finding-to-organ location does not license the inverse organ-to-finding triple.
A qualifier-to-finding relation and a finding-to-site relation form a path; they do not imply qualifier-to-site.

principles.instruction: For a standalone, unmodified, adjective-first verbless sentence in the FINDINGS section consisting only of a state observation immediately followed by an anatomical noun, emit LocatedAt from the anatomical entity to the state entity; otherwise retain the canonical hosted finding/state/device -> anatomical host direction.

current_principles.instruction: Project every relation onto the supplied predicted-entity inventory. A relation endpoint must be the ID of one supplied predicted entity; never invent an ID, create a composite span, or return a human-annotation ID.
current_principles.applies_when: Selecting or aligning either endpoint of any relation.
exceptions: Minor punctuation or boundary differences may be normalized when a predicted entity clearly denotes the same concept.
A predicted entity may be used despite an observation-label disagreement if its span and concept clearly match.

If an annotated multiword endpoint is split into several predicted entities, select the single semantic head appropriate to the relation. Additional modifier-to-head relations may be emitted only when independently licensed by the text.
If no predicted entity represents a required endpoint, omit that relation rather than substituting a neighboring entity or collapsing a relation path.
examples: A location spanning a regional qualifier plus an organ maps to the supplied organ-head entity, while the regional qualifier may separately Modify the organ.
If a positional predicate is not supplied as an entity, do not replace it with the finding and manufacture a direct positional relation.

current_principles.instruction: Emit directed triples with exactly one allowed predicate: LocatedAt, Modify, or SuggestiveOf. Preserve subject and object roles; do not add inverse, symmetric, or transitive relations. Emit an exact triple only once.
current_principles.applies_when: Formatting and validating all relation outputs.
exceptions: The same endpoint pair may receive different predicates only when distinct textual semantics independently support both labels.
Repeated mentions in different sentences or report sections are separate entities and may receive analogous relations without being duplicates.
examples: A finding-to-organ location does not license the inverse organ-to-finding triple.
A qualifier-to-finding relation and a finding-to-site relation form a path; they do not imply qualifier-to-site.

current_principles.instruction: For a standalone, unmodified, adjective-first verbless sentence in the FINDINGS section consisting only of a state observation immediately followed by an anatomical noun, emit LocatedAt from the anatomical entity to the state entity; otherwise retain the canonical hosted finding/state/device -> anatomical host direction.
current_principles.applies_when: The local FINDINGS sentence has the complete form "<state observation> <anatomy>." with no copula, coordination, anatomical modifier, or other supplied content entity.
exceptions: Copular or anatomy-first predications retain state -> anatomy direction.
Adjective-first fragments containing laterality, regional qualifiers, coordination, or additional content retain state -> anatomy direction.
Summary or IMPRESSION restatements retain state -> anatomy direction.
examples: In the standalone FINDINGS fragment "Clear lungs.", emit lungs -> Clear.
For the IMPRESSION fragment "Clear lungs.", emit Clear -> lungs.

current_principles.instruction: Represent anatomical phrases compositionally. When selecting the LocatedAt object from a phrase containing an anatomy-bearing owner or descriptor plus a generic depiction/container noun such as contour, silhouette, region, or zone, attach the observation to the anatomy-bearing entity rather than the generic noun. Continue to attach anatomical qualifiers to their head with Modify when independently licensed.
current_principles.applies_when: A LocatedAt candidate has competing supplied objects within the same anatomical noun phrase, and one candidate identifies the anatomy while another merely names its generic depiction or regional container.
exceptions: Use a specific anatomical head such as lobe, spine, atrium, or hemidiaphragm when it is the actual asserted site; laterality or directional modifiers do not displace such a head solely because they are closer.

Retain the generic property/component as object when the subject explicitly denotes a property-specific measurement or alteration of that component, such as an enlarged silhouette; scalar property predications involving size or volume remain governed by R06.

Do not attach the observation to a distant anatomy mentioned in a proximity phrase such as "near the hilum" when the observation is locally anchored to an anatomy-bearing descriptor in its own noun phrase.

current_principles.instruction: Use SuggestiveOf for an explicit evidential or interpretive link from an observed sign, finding, structure, or state to a possible diagnosis, explanation, consequence, or clinical interpretation. Resolve an omitted evidence source to the immediately preceding finding when an adjacent inferential sentence uses a demonstrative, ellipsis, or contrastive alternative without introducing a new source; when a postposed inferential phrase scopes over a coordinated evidence phrase, emit the relation from each eligible conjunct.

exceptions: The target should normally be an observation or interpretive entity, not a purely anatomical entity.

An anatomical source is permitted when the anatomy or its appearance is explicitly placed within the inferential scope.
Do not use SuggestiveOf for recommendations, follow-up examinations, or mere co-occurrence.

examples: single imaging finding -> first possible diagnosis and single imaging finding -> second possible diagnosis

current_principles.instruction: Relation annotation is independent of assertion status. Preserve valid LocatedAt, Modify, and SuggestiveOf links for present, absent, uncertain, stable, or negated findings.
current_principles.applies_when: A relation-bearing phrase occurs under negation, uncertainty, or an absence label.
exceptions: Negation does not by itself license a relation; the underlying semantic link must still be explicit.
Do not convert negation words into relation endpoints unless they are supplied entities and function as genuine modifiers.
examples: absent effusion -> pleural compartment
acute qualifier -> absent abnormality
absent opacities -> possible diagnosis when the sentence explicitly states what such opacities would suggest

current_principles.instruction: Resolve shared scope conservatively. A common state or modifier may relate to multiple coordinated entities when grammar clearly places all conjuncts within its scope.
current_principles.applies_when: A predicate follows or precedes a coordinated list of findings, structures, or properties.
exceptions: Do not extend the predicate to a nearby entity outside the coordination.
Do not assume that a relation applying to one repeated finding automatically applies to all other mentions.
examples: one normality state -> each explicitly coordinated organ property
one unremarkable state -> each member of an anatomical list
one finding -> general site and a more specific site when both are explicitly asserted

current_principles.instruction: Keep relation resolution local. Prefer entities in the same noun phrase, clause, or explicit predicate-argument construction, and do not perform unsupported cross-sentence or cross-section coreference.
current_principles.applies_when: A possible relation would require resolving a pronoun, an omitted noun, a distant repeated concept, or an antecedent in another section.
exceptions: Repeated findings in a summary section may be annotated independently using the entities and wording present in that section.
A relation may cross a short clause boundary only when the source and target are explicitly connected by the sentence's grammar.
examples: Do not connect an earlier lesion to a later diagnosis expressed only through an unannotated pronoun.
Annotate a repeated summary finding with its own summary-site entity rather than linking it to the earlier site mention.

current_principles.instruction: When a supplied positional or projection predicate is an entity, preserve it as an intermediate relation node. Link the positional predicate to its anatomical destination with LocatedAt, and use Modify for its direct compositional attachment to the finding or device component.
current_principles.applies_when: The text contains a supplied entity corresponding to projecting, overlying, or another positional relation.
exceptions: Do not collapse the path into a direct finding-to-site relation unless the text independently states that direct location.
If the positional entity is unavailable, omit relations requiring it rather than replacing it with an adjacent entity.
Use the grammatical descriptive dependency for the Modify edge; do not infer both directions.
examples: positional predicate -> destination structure via LocatedAt
positional predicate -> device tip via Modify when the predicate describes the tip
finding and positional predicate form a compositional edge only when both are supplied entities

current_principles.instruction: Choose the predicate by semantic precedence: explicit diagnostic interpretation selects SuggestiveOf; explicit spatial or host anchoring selects LocatedAt; descriptive or compositional dependence selects Modify.
current_principles.applies_when: A candidate pair appears compatible with more than one relation label.
exceptions: Multiple labels may be retained only if separate explicit constructions support separate meanings.
Entity labels alone never determine the predicate.
Corpus-specific direction anomalies should not override the dominant semantic direction unless the local text unambiguously requires it.
examples: A lesion described as nodular receives Modify from the morphology term, but a possible nodule interpretation receives SuggestiveOf.
An anatomical adjective on a lesion is a location anchor, whereas the same adjective on an anatomical head is a modifier.

current_principles.instruction: Avoid relation overgeneration. Do not annotate mere adjacency, shared topic, comparison with a prior study, examination recommendations, notification statements, or transitive consequences of already emitted relations.
current_principles.applies_when: No explicit grammatical, spatial, descriptive, or inferential link connects two supplied entities.
exceptions: Measurements and explicit temporal-status descriptors are valid Modify relations.
Explicit report-summary restatements are valid independent relation contexts.
examples: A recommended imaging region is not automatically related to the finding prompting the recommendation.
A modifier attached to a finding does not inherit the finding's anatomical location.
Two findings listed in the same sentence receive no relation solely because they co-occur.

current_principles.instruction: Do not emit Modify when the subject functions only as an epistemic or metalinguistic assessment of a concept's reality, determinacy, or clinical significance rather than as a descriptive attribute of that concept.
current_principles.applies_when: A supplied term such as "true," "indeterminate," or "unknown" qualifies whether a finding is real or interpretable, or comments on its clinical significance.
exceptions: Retain Modify for explicit morphology, measurement, severity, temporal status, and scalar degree descriptors, including terms such as rounded, nodular, stable, significant, and borderline.

principles.instruction: Project every relation onto the supplied predicted-entity inventory. A relation endpoint must be the ID of one supplied predicted entity; never invent an ID, create a composite span, or return a human-annotation ID.
principles.applies_when: Selecting or aligning either endpoint of any relation.
exceptions: Minor punctuation or boundary differences may be normalized when a predicted entity clearly denotes the same concept.
A predicted entity may be used despite an observation-label disagreement if its span and concept clearly match.

If an annotated multiword endpoint is split into several predicted entities, select the single semantic head appropriate to the relation. Additional modifier-to-head relations may be emitted only when independently licensed by the text.
If no predicted entity represents a required endpoint, omit that relation rather than substituting a neighboring entity or collapsing a relation path.
examples: A location spanning a regional qualifier plus an organ maps to the supplied organ-head entity, while the regional qualifier may separately Modify the organ.
If a positional predicate is not supplied as an entity, do not replace it with the finding and manufacture a direct positional relation.

principles.instruction: Emit directed triples with exactly one allowed predicate: LocatedAt, Modify, or SuggestiveOf. Preserve subject and object roles; do not add inverse, symmetric, or transitive relations. Emit an exact triple only once.
principles.applies_when: Formatting and validating all relation outputs.
exceptions: The same endpoint pair may receive different predicates only when distinct textual semantics independently support both labels.
Repeated mentions in different sentences or report sections are separate entities and may receive analogous relations without being duplicates.
examples: A finding-to-organ location does not license the inverse organ-to-finding triple.
A qualifier-to-finding relation and a finding-to-site relation form a path; they do not imply qualifier-to-site.

principles.instruction: Use LocatedAt when the subject is spatially, anatomically, or functionally anchored to the object. The subject is normally a finding, state, device, device component, material, or positional observation; the object is normally the anatomical site, region, structure, or property that hosts it.
principles.applies_when: The text explicitly assigns a finding or state to a body location, anatomical descriptor, organ property, or device destination.

For an anatomical adjective attached to an observation, such as an organ-system adjective attached to a lesion, direct the relation from the observation to the anatomical adjective.

normality or clarity state -> organ or organ property
device tip -> destination structure

principles.instruction: Represent anatomical phrases compositionally. Use Modify from laterality, level, segment, ordinal, directional, or regional qualifiers to the anatomical head. Attach a finding to the anatomical head with LocatedAt unless the text explicitly anchors it to another supplied component.

exceptions: Do not attach the finding independently to every word in a location phrase.
A property noun such as size, contour, silhouette, or volume may participate in the property convention in R06 rather than behaving as an ordinary regional qualifier.
If an explicit local construction makes a qualifier itself the immediate anchor, a relation chain may be retained, but this must not be inferred merely from token proximity.
examples: laterality -> lobe and level -> lobe via Modify; opacity -> lobe via LocatedAt

directional and ordinal rib qualifiers -> rib via Modify

principles.instruction: Use Modify for descriptive, restrictive, quantitative, or compositional dependence. The subject is the qualifier or dependent concept, and the object is the entity whose meaning it narrows or completes.
principles.applies_when: One supplied entity expresses degree, severity, morphology, distribution, temporal status, certainty, measurement, type, or another nonspatial property of another entity.
exceptions: Do not use Modify for a finding-to-anatomy association; use LocatedAt.
Do not use Modify for a finding-to-diagnostic interpretation; use SuggestiveOf.
When a degree word modifies another qualifier, preserve the chain rather than attaching both directly to the final finding.
Noun-complement constructions must be interpreted semantically rather than by word order alone; use Modify only when the two entities form one compositional concept.
examples: severity qualifier -> finding
measurement -> lesion
morphology qualifier -> opacity
degree adverb -> descriptive adjective -> finding
chronicity or acuity qualifier -> disease or abnormality

In constructions equivalent to an organ's size, contour, silhouette, or similar property, use Modify from the property/component noun to the anatomical owner. exceptions: If the property token itself is the explicit host of the state, the state may be LocatedAt the property rather than the broader organ.

An ordinary anatomical qualifier such as laterality or segment follows R04 instead.
examples: size property -> organ via Modify; normal state -> organ or size via LocatedAt
contour or silhouette property -> anatomical owner via Modify

principles.instruction: Attach every explicit modifier directly to its intended head. Multiple parallel qualifiers may share one head, while nested qualifiers form a chain according to scope.

examples: measurement -> lesion and morphology -> lesion
severity -> change and degenerative type -> change

principles.instruction: Use SuggestiveOf for an explicit evidential or interpretive link from an observed sign, finding, structure, or state to a possible diagnosis, explanation, consequence, or clinical interpretation. The source is the evidence-bearing entity and the object is the inferred concept.
principles.applies_when: The text uses an inferential construction equivalent to suggesting, representing, being consistent with, demonstrating, possibly being, or having uncertain significance.
exceptions: The target should normally be an observation or interpretive entity, not a purely anatomical entity.
An anatomical source is permitted when the anatomy or its appearance is explicitly said to support an inferred condition.

examples: single imaging finding -> first possible diagnosis and single imaging finding -> second possible diagnosis

principles.instruction: Resolve shared scope conservatively. A common state or modifier may relate to multiple coordinated entities when grammar clearly places all conjuncts within its scope.

one unremarkable state -> each member of an anatomical list

principles.instruction: Keep relation resolution local. Prefer entities in the same noun phrase, clause, or explicit predicate-argument construction, and do not perform unsupported cross-sentence or cross-section coreference.
principles.applies_when: A possible relation would require resolving a pronoun, an omitted noun, a distant repeated concept, or an antecedent in another section.
exceptions: Repeated findings in a summary section may be annotated independently using the entities and wording present in that section.

principles.instruction: Annotate report content in the diagnostic finding and conclusion portions. Do not annotate examination headers, acquisition metadata, clinical-history/indication text, comparison text, or redaction placeholders.
principles.applies_when: Processing a structured imaging report.
exceptions: Anatomical locations mentioned in a conclusion, recommendation, notification, or follow-up statement remain eligible when they are part of the report assessment.
A repeated finding is annotated again at each textual occurrence, including when restated in the conclusion.
examples: A diagnosis named only as the reason for examination is not marked; the same diagnosis discussed as an imaging assessment is eligible.
A body region named in a recommendation for additional imaging is eligible as anatomy.

principles.instruction: Use ANAT for anatomical structures, body regions, compartments, tissue types, and anatomical localization components.
principles.applies_when: A token or phrase component denotes where a finding is located or the bodily structure being described.
exceptions: Do not use ANAT for a device, surgical procedure, device feature, or finding merely because it is adjacent to anatomy.
A word with a non-anatomical role is not ANAT even if it can occur in anatomical expressions.
examples: Laterality, level, direction, position, and regional terms in a location expression are each anatomical components.
Organ names, lobes, vessels, bones, spaces, contours, silhouettes, and anatomical size descriptors can be ANAT.

principles.instruction: Split composite anatomical expressions into their separately meaningful lexical components rather than creating one maximal anatomy span.
principles.applies_when: A multiword location contains laterality, orientation, level, region, structure, or tissue words.
exceptions: Keep a lexical unit intact when its measurement or observation descriptor is conventionally expressed as one unit.
Do not create entities for intervening function words, conjunctions, articles, or punctuation solely to bridge components.
examples: A location containing side, vertical position, and organ receives separate ANAT spans for those components.
A compound cardiopulmonary region may be one ANAT span when presented as one inseparable lexical descriptor.

principles.instruction: Use OBS-DP for a definitely asserted observation, whether abnormal, normal, stable, postoperative, or device-related.
principles.applies_when: The report directly states or affirms an imaging finding, morphology, measurement, quantity, change, normality, position, device, or procedure-related result.
exceptions: Do not assign OBS-DP merely because a word is medically salient; use OBS-U when the finding is explicitly hedged and OBS-DA when directly denied.
A body-structure word remains ANAT even when the associated observation is OBS-DP.
examples: Measurements, shapes, opacity-like appearances, changes over time, severity, distribution, normality, and clear/unremarkable status are OBS-DP.
Device type, device tip, placement descriptors, surgical material, surgery-related state, and amputation-related state are OBS-DP rather than ANAT.

principles.instruction: Use OBS-DA for the finding target explicitly placed under definite negation or exclusion.
principles.applies_when: A direct negative construction denies a finding, pathology, abnormality, or clinically meaningful qualifier.
exceptions: Retain ANAT for the anatomical site within a negative statement.
Do not label negation cue words, absence verbs, or generic syntax by themselves.

In negative-evidence constructions, the directly denied evidence/target is OBS-DA; an embedded descriptive phrase may remain OBS-DP if it is analyzed as the described observation rather than the direct negated target.
examples: A denied fluid collection, collapsed-lung finding, consolidation, or acute abnormality is OBS-DA.
Qualifiers that form part of the directly denied finding, such as extent or acuity, are normally OBS-DA as separate spans.

principles.instruction: Use OBS-U for an observation, diagnosis, etiology, or significance that the report presents as possible, suggested, indeterminate, artifactual, or otherwise unresolved.
principles.applies_when: The local assertion is qualified by uncertainty, possibility, conditional interpretation, unknown significance, or a diagnostic alternative.
exceptions: Do not propagate uncertainty from a candidate diagnosis to adjacent anatomy or to a separately established observation.
A mere coordinated alternative does not automatically make every term OBS-U; use the explicit assertion context and the local semantic role.
Do not use OBS-U for an established chronic or historical finding when it is directly asserted in that occurrence.
examples: A suspected infection, possible malignancy, potential nodal process, possible artifact, or suggested metastatic process is OBS-U.
The same disease term can be OBS-U in a hedged discussion and OBS-DP in a later definitive conclusion.

principles.instruction: Determine OBS-DP, OBS-DA, and OBS-U independently for each lexical observation component; do not force an entire noun phrase to share one label.
principles.applies_when: A finding phrase combines anatomy, morphology, measurement, diagnostic nouns, qualifiers, or different certainty scopes.
exceptions: Use the local grammatical and assertion scope rather than a global sentence-level polarity when these differ.
When a modifier is only contextual or temporal rather than part of the denied target, it may remain OBS-DP despite a neighboring negative statement.
examples: An uncertain diagnostic noun can coexist with an ANAT site and a definitely present morphology or measurement.
A direct negative statement may contain an ANAT site, an absent target, and separately annotated descriptive material.

principles.instruction: Annotate clinically meaningful observation descriptors at fine granularity, including measurements, numeric dimensions, shape, density/opacity, distribution, chronicity, severity, stability, interval change, projection, and procedural/device descriptors.
principles.applies_when: Such a descriptor contributes an imaging observation or materially characterizes one.
exceptions: Do not annotate purely grammatical words or unsupported reporting verbs.
Do not annotate a recommendation action, modality name, or administrative notification merely because it occurs near an observation.
examples: A dimension expression including its unit is one OBS-DP span; adjacent shape and finding-type terms are separate OBS-DP spans.
A multiword descriptor of texture or degenerative change is generally split into its meaningful descriptor and finding components.

principles.instruction: Resolve context-sensitive words by their role in the current phrase, not by a fixed lexicon.
principles.applies_when: A term can denote anatomy in one context and an observation, device feature, or descriptor in another.
exceptions: Anatomical size, contour, or silhouette components are ANAT when they identify a body structure or structural attribute.
Size, shape, level, tip, centrality, or distal position is OBS-DP when it describes a lesion, device, or finding rather than anatomy.
examples: A structural contour may be ANAT, while a lesion's size is OBS-DP.
A tissue adjective can be ANAT when it names the structure being assessed and OBS-DP when it functions as a finding descriptor.

principles.instruction: Use exact, non-normalized half-open character offsets; entity spans must contain only the lexical entity token(s) and must exclude adjacent sentence punctuation such as periods and commas.
principles.applies_when: Producing entity spans.
exceptions: Include punctuation only when it is an intrinsic, source-tokenized part of the lexical entity itself.
Whitespace and section delimiters are excluded.
